newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Winterthur to consolidate Neuenburger. [CORRECTED 09:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Winterthur to consolidate Neuenburger. [CORRECTED 09:00 GMT]

text.p: Swiss insurer Winterthur said it would take over the remaining business of subsidiary Neuenburger and consolidate the unit under a new, unified Swiss domestic management in the course of 1997. (Corrects to make clear that Winterthur is consolidating all of Neuenburger)
A Winterthur statement said the move would result in the loss of 150 jobs out of around 800 at Neuenburg.

The Swiss streamlining affects business units Winterthur Insurance, Winterthur Life, Swissline, Federal, Winterthur Legal Protection as well as Neuenburger, which Wintherthur took full ownership of last April.

Winterthur said functions now performed at Neuenburger's head office would be moved to other locations. In return, many Winterthur jobs covering French-speaking western Swizterland would be moved to the canton of Neuchatel (Neuenburg).
"Despite all these efforts, approximately 150 redundancies will be unavoidable in Neuchatel," the statement said.
Neuenburger, known in French as Neuchatel, is an all-line carrier with its own sales force covering the full swiss market.
"In view of the market developments, it is quite conceivable that Neuchatel could soon be facing considerable cost problems," Winterthur said.
"This is why its business will be integrated into Winterthur's portfolio in the cource of next year," it added.

The integration of Neuenburger was part of a plan announced in July to concentrate Winterthur's business units in Switzerland, apart from the multinational large customer business, under a single management group.
The Swiss streamlining affects buiness units Winterthur Protection as well as Neuenburger, which Winterthur took full ownership of last April.

Winterthur said functions now performed at Neuenburger's head office would be moved to other locations. In return, many Winterthur jobs covering French-speaking western Switzerland would be moved to the canton of Neuchatel (Neuenburg).
"Despite all these efforts, approximately 150 redundancies will be unavoidable in Neuchatel," the statement said.
Neuenburger and Winterthur had earlier merged their business activities outside of Switzerland, said Johannes Schaller from Winterthur investor relations.
"Now we are thinking about whether to preserve the brand name Neuchatel, especially bwcause it is known in international transport insurance," he told Reuters.
Neueburger has 20 percent of the transport insurance market in Switzerland and has other important markets in France, Germany, Italy and Austria.
Winterthur said the consolidation of Neuenvurger could not wait any longer because considerable new investments would have been needed soon in areas such as information technology.

"Neuchatel would not have been able to maintain its current market share in non-life business of merely approximately 1.9 percent," said Winterthur, which with 22 percent is the biggest non-life insurer in Switzerland.
